sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带上300件最珍贵的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, it was a young Canadian data expert who came up with the plan to harvest people's personal data off Facebook and use it to influence their voting behavior.
sentences.zh: 今天，一位年轻的加拿大数据专家想出了一个计划，从Facebook上抓取人们的个人数据，并利用这些数据来影响他们的投票行为。

sentences.en: Why the brains behind Cambridge Analytica is now the whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 为什么剑桥分析公司（Cambridge Analytica）背后的智囊现在成了举报人？

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月21日，星期三。

sentences.en: Matt, when did you first get introduced to Christopher Wiley?
sentences.zh: 马特，你是什么时候第一次见到克里斯托弗·威利的？

sentences.en: So I was in London in August and a reporter wanted to introduce us to this kid, Christopher Wiley, who had been one of the people who helped found Cambridge Analytica.
sentences.zh: 那是8月，当时我在伦敦，一位记者想把我们介绍给这个叫克里斯托弗·威利的年轻人，他曾是剑桥分析公司的创始人之一。

sentences.en: Matt Rosenberg was one of the reporters who broke the story of Cambridge Analytica.
sentences.zh: 马特·罗森伯格是率先报道剑桥分析公司丑闻的记者之一。

sentences.en: We met in East London.
sentences.zh: 我们在伦敦东区见了面。

sentences.en: I was staying at this hotel, this kind of hip hotel in East London.
sentences.zh: 当时我住在伦敦东区一家挺时髦的酒店里。

sentences.en: And in walks this guy.
sentences.zh: 然后这家伙就走了进来。

sentences.en: He's like this skinny, sort of hipsterish, 20-year-old East London kid who was a vegan from Canada.
sentences.zh: 他看起来就像个瘦瘦的、有点嬉皮士风格的20岁伦敦东区小伙，还是个来自加拿大的素食主义者。

sentences.en: He's wearing a beanie from the Obama 2012 inauguration.
sentences.zh: 他戴着一顶奥巴马2012年就职典礼的针织帽。

sentences.en: And he's coming there to tell us all about how he helped found this firm that, you know,
sentences.zh: 他来这里是为了告诉我们，他如何帮助创立了那家公司，你知道的，

sentences.en: was supposed to be the arsenal of weapons in Steve Bannon's culture war to reshape America into a right-wing nationalist country.
sentences.zh: 那家公司本应成为史蒂夫·班农文化战争中的武器库，旨在将美国重塑为一个右翼民族主义国家。

sentences.en: And what was interesting about this guy's story?
sentences.zh: 这个人的故事有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: Why did you care what he had to say?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会在意他要说的话？

sentences.en: So, you know, by the summer of 2017, we all knew Cambridge Analytica had worked for the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到2017年夏天，我们都知道剑桥分析公司曾为特朗普竞选团队工作过。

sentences.en: We also knew that there had been Facebook data somehow used by this company.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道这家公司以某种方式使用了Facebook的数据。

sentences.en: But what Chris had to say was that it was tens of millions of profiles.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯要说的是，涉及的数据多达数千万份个人资料。

sentences.en: It was a scale and a scope of data harvesting that we did not know.
sentences.zh: 这种数据抓取的规模和范围是我们此前所不知道的。

sentences.en: So Chris understood how Cambridge Analytica had used Facebook in a way that hadn't yet been disclosed or understood by the public.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯了解剑桥分析公司是如何使用Facebook的，其方式在当时尚未被公众披露或理解。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he was integral to it.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为他是其中的核心人物。

sentences.en: So you're at this bar in London with Christopher Wiley.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时在伦敦的一家酒吧里和克里斯托弗·威利在一起。

sentences.en: What's the story that he tells you?
sentences.zh: 他告诉你的故事是什么？

sentences.en: I kind of tell him to start at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我让他从头讲起。

sentences.en: He is a high school dropout from British Columbia in Canada.
sentences.zh: 他是一名来自加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省的高中辍学生。

sentences.en: He left high school after suing the school district over inclusion issues.
sentences.zh: 他在起诉学区关于包容性问题后离开了高中。

sentences.en: Chris is gay, very openly so.
sentences.zh: 克里斯是同性恋，而且非常公开。

sentences.en: After dropping out, he drifted to Ottawa where he started working for the Liberal Party in Canada.
sentences.zh: 辍学后，他漂泊到了渥太华，开始为加拿大自由党工作。

sentences.en: And there he met Ken Strasma, who was Obama's big data guy in 2008.
sentences.zh: 在那里他遇到了肯·斯特拉斯马，他是2008年奥巴马竞选团队的大数据专家。

sentences.en: And Ken kind of became his mentor and taught him about data science and using it for elections.
sentences.zh: 肯成了他的导师，教他数据科学以及如何将其用于选举。

sentences.en: And after a while, though, he kind of wanted to go back to school.
sentences.zh: 不过过了一段时间，他还是想回到学校。

sentences.en: He gets into the London School of Economics and heads over to London.
sentences.zh: 他考进了伦敦政治经济学院，于是前往伦敦。

sentences.en: But while he's there, I mean, he has this seeming kind of passion or compulsion to do political data.
sentences.zh: 但在那儿的时候，我的意思是，他似乎有一种做政治数据的热情或强迫症。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like being in the mall, but he got sucked back into the data world.
sentences.zh: 就像在商场里一样，但他又被吸回了数据世界。

sentences.en: And ends up with this company called SCL Elections.
sentences.zh: 最终加入了一家叫SCL Elections的公司。

sentences.en: Now, SCL Elections is part of a bigger company called the SCL Group, which does a lot of defense and intelligence contracting.
sentences.zh: SCL Elections是一家名为SCL集团的大型公司的一部分，该集团承接了大量国防和情报合同。

sentences.en: It's like a research communications company.
sentences.zh: 它就像一家研究传播公司。

sentences.en: And SCL Elections, their election division, is just a small part of this company.
sentences.zh: 而SCL Elections，也就是他们的选举部门，只是这家公司的一小部分。

sentences.en: But it's run by this guy, Alexander Nix, who is this very posh Brit.
sentences.zh: 但它是由一个叫亚历山大·尼克斯的人经营的，他是一个非常讲究的英国人。

sentences.en: And Alexander Nix really wants to get a bigger chunk of the American kind of political market.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·尼克斯非常想在美国政治市场分得更大的一杯羹。

sentences.en: He wants to break into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他想打入美国市场。

sentences.en: He really wants to break into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他非常想打入美国市场。

sentences.en: And Nix is on a flight from London to New York and has this completely happenstance meeting with some people who work for Herman Cain.
sentences.zh: 尼克斯在从伦敦飞往纽约的航班上，偶然遇到了几个为赫尔曼·凯恩工作的人。

sentences.en: The Republican presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 那位共和党总统候选人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And through them, they get into the world of the kind of far right of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 通过他们，他们进入了共和党极右翼的世界。

sentences.en: And that eventually leads Nix and Wiley and the small data team they've assembled to Steve Bannon and Robert Mercer.
sentences.zh: 这最终将尼克斯、威利以及他们组建的小型数据团队引向了史蒂夫·班农和罗伯特·默瑟。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The kind of kings of American conservative politics.
sentences.zh: 他们算是美国保守派政治的王者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Nix and Wiley get to know the Mercers and Steve Bannon, whose Breitbart empire is exploding and he's now setting up Breitbart, U.K.,
sentences.zh: 尼克斯和威利结识了默瑟家族和史蒂夫·班农，班农的布赖特巴特新闻网（Breitbart）帝国正在迅速扩张，他当时正在筹建布赖特巴特英国分部，

sentences.en: and really wants to reshape American politics.
sentences.zh: 并且非常想重塑美国政治。

sentences.en: And how are they going to do this?
sentences.zh: 他们打算怎么做呢？

sentences.en: So they've got this idea that they are going to take a new field of study called psychographic research.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个想法，就是采用一种名为“心理测绘研究”的新研究领域。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And they are going to sell the Mercers and Bannon on this idea of creating a political data firm.
sentences.zh: 他们打算向默瑟家族和班农兜售这个创建政治数据公司的想法。

sentences.en: And instead of going out and polling people on, like, what issue, what do you support on gun control?
sentences.zh: 与其出去对人们进行民意调查，问他们支持什么议题，比如枪支管制？

sentences.en: Or what do you think about taxes?
sentences.zh: 或者你对税收有什么看法？

sentences.en: You're going to go out and you're going to figure out the actual personalities, what emotionally drives each American voter.
sentences.zh: 不如直接去找出每个美国选民真实的个性，以及是什么在情感上驱动着他们。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And you're going to tailor messages to them.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以为他们量身定制信息。

sentences.en: And through that, you're going to be able to predict their voter behavior.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，你将能够预测他们的投票行为。

sentences.en: You're going to be able to influence them.
sentences.zh: 你将能够影响他们。

sentences.en: It's that whole idea, that Breitbart idea of kind of politics being downstream of culture.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个整体理念，即布赖特巴特那种“政治是文化的下游”的观点。

sentences.en: That if you want to change the politics, you can change the culture.
sentences.zh: 如果你想改变政治，你就可以改变文化。

sentences.en: And that psychographics is this key to doing so.
sentences.zh: 而心理测绘就是实现这一点的关键。

sentences.en: And Matt, where did this idea of psychographic research come from?
sentences.zh: 马特，这种心理测绘研究的想法是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: This had originated a few years earlier at Cambridge University.
sentences.zh: 这起源于几年前的剑桥大学。

sentences.en: They had something called the Psychographic Center, which is dedicated to this idea of using big data to kind of map personalities.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个叫“心理测绘中心”的机构，致力于利用大数据来绘制个性图谱。

sentences.en: So Chris had been hanging around this center.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯一直在这个中心附近转悠。

sentences.en: And at that center, a graduate student had developed this technique to kind of predict personalities by looking at Facebook likes.
sentences.zh: 在那里，一名研究生开发了一种技术，通过查看Facebook的点赞记录来预测个性。

sentences.en: And this grad student had done this study where he had gone through Facebook and harvested likes.
sentences.zh: 这位研究生做了一项研究，他通过Facebook抓取了点赞数据。

sentences.en: And at this point, Facebook was wide open.
sentences.zh: 当时，Facebook是完全开放的。

sentences.en: Likes by default were public.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下，点赞是公开的。

sentences.en: So scraping them was very easy.
sentences.zh: 所以抓取它们非常容易。

sentences.en: And he found that on an average of 68 likes, he could predict amazing things like your skin color with 95% accuracy, your sexual orientation with 85% accuracy.
sentences.zh: 他发现，平均只需68个点赞，他就能以95%的准确率预测出惊人的信息，比如你的肤色，以85%的准确率预测出你的性取向。

sentences.en: You know, these guys that developed this technique that they claimed could reveal a tremendous amount of people's personalities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些开发出这种技术的人声称，它能揭示人们大量的个性信息。

sentences.en: You give them 70 likes and they would know you better than your friends.
sentences.zh: 你给他们70个点赞，他们就比你的朋友更了解你。

sentences.en: At 150, better than your parents.
sentences.zh: 达到150个，就比你的父母更了解你。

sentences.en: At 300, better than your own partners.
sentences.zh: 达到300个，就比你的伴侣更了解你。

sentences.en: So this research said that through 300 likes, you could be known by an outsider better than your own spouse.
sentences.zh: 所以这项研究表明，通过300个点赞，外人就能比你的配偶更了解你。

sentences.en: Pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多是这样。

sentences.en: You know, after kind of harvesting all this Facebook data, they would unleash the algorithms that had been developed and kind of create all kinds of correlations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在抓取了所有这些Facebook数据后，他们会释放出开发好的算法，并建立各种相关性。

sentences.en: So they'd find like, let's say you liked Hello Kitty, the Hello Kitty brand.
sentences.zh: 比如，假设你点赞了Hello Kitty这个品牌。

sentences.en: They found what they claimed was a lot of accuracy, that you were probably a very open-minded person but not particularly conscientious.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，他们声称准确率很高，你可能是一个思想非常开放但不太有责任心的人。

sentences.en: If you like the Wu-Tang Clan, you're a heterosexual male, so guilty as charged.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢武当派（Wu-Tang Clan），那你就是个异性恋男性，好吧，我中招了。

sentences.en: And, you know, they claimed people's personalities could be simply measured through Facebook likes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们声称人们的个性可以通过Facebook点赞简单地衡量出来。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Chris sees this and he's like, well, we can do this.
sentences.zh: 克里斯看到了这一点，心想，好吧，我们也能做到。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: At the same time, he's kind of hanging around this center learning about this,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他一直在这个中心附近学习这些东西，

sentences.en: SCL is working with the Mercers on a small pilot project to kind of test psychographics in the Virginia 2013 gubernatorial race.
sentences.zh: SCL正在与默瑟家族合作一个小型的试点项目，旨在测试2013年弗吉尼亚州州长竞选中的心理测绘。

sentences.en: You had Ken Cuccinelli, the Republican, who they were backing, running against Terry McAuliffe, who was a Democrat, who eventually won.
sentences.zh: 当时共和党人肯·库奇内利是他们支持的对象，他与最终获胜的民主党人特里·麦考利夫竞选。

sentences.en: They weren't using any of the Facebook data for this.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有为此使用任何Facebook数据。

sentences.en: They were trying to use polling data and other kinds of data to measure personality.
sentences.zh: 他们试图使用民调数据和其他类型的数据来衡量个性。

sentences.en: The results were ambiguous but promising enough that the Mercers said, you know what, let's go ahead.
sentences.zh: 结果模棱两可，但足够有前景，以至于默瑟家族说，你知道吗，我们继续吧。

sentences.en: We're going to try and create a new company here.
sentences.zh: 我们要在这里创建一家新公司。

sentences.en: That focused on the idea of psychographic research.
sentences.zh: 专注于心理测绘研究的想法。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then by June of 2014, the Mercers had put in about $15 million.
sentences.zh: 到了2014年6月，默瑟家族已经投入了大约1500万美元。

sentences.en: You know, Steve Bannon was on the board, one of the co-founders.
sentences.zh: 你知道，史蒂夫·班农是董事会成员，也是联合创始人之一。

sentences.en: And these guys suddenly had a problem because it was easy enough to get that kind of polling data and all kinds of other data points you needed to kind of measure personality in some small Virginia counties.
sentences.zh: 这些人突然遇到了一个问题，因为在弗吉尼亚州的一些小县城里，获取那种民调数据和衡量个性所需的其他数据点很容易。

sentences.en: You know, they'd only tested two counties in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们只测试了弗吉尼亚州的两个县。

sentences.en: Getting that kind of data on a national scale was just – they didn't have the resources to do it or the time.
sentences.zh: 要在全国范围内获取那种数据，他们根本没有资源或时间。

sentences.en: But Chris, because he had been hanging around Cambridge, knew that there was a data set out there that could work to measure personality.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯因为一直在剑桥大学附近转悠，知道有一个数据集可以用来衡量个性。

sentences.en: And that was that Facebook data that the young PhD student had been playing around with.
sentences.zh: 那就是那位年轻的博士生一直在摆弄的Facebook数据。

sentences.en: The psychographic center, though, wouldn't play ball.
sentences.zh: 不过，心理测绘中心不愿配合。

sentences.en: And give that data over.
sentences.zh: 不愿交出那些数据。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they found a professor familiar with the research also at Cambridge University, an assistant psychology professor named Alexander Kogan.
sentences.zh: 所以他们找到了另一位熟悉这项研究的教授，同样在剑桥大学，一位名叫亚历山大·科根的心理学助理教授。

sentences.en: He's a Russian-American.
sentences.zh: 他是俄裔美国人。

sentences.en: And he agrees to do it.
sentences.zh: 他同意了。

sentences.en: He agrees to kind of recreate the data set.
sentences.zh: 他同意重新创建那个数据集。

sentences.en: So here's how it worked.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: People would take a personality quiz.
sentences.zh: 人们会参加一个性格测试。

sentences.en: And I think it's really important to note when listeners hear Facebook quiz,
sentences.zh: 我认为当听众听到“Facebook测试”时，有一点非常重要，需要说明，

sentences.en: they're thinking some kind of quiz like what kind of root vegetable are you or which game are thrown into the characters.
sentences.zh: 他们会想到那种测试，比如“你是哪种根茎类蔬菜”或者“你是哪种游戏角色”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's not what was going on here.
sentences.zh: 这里的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: They're told that this is for academic research.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知这是为了学术研究。

sentences.en: They would get paid a small sum to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们会因为做这个测试而得到一小笔报酬。

sentences.en: A very standard personality quiz.
sentences.zh: 一个非常标准的性格测试。

sentences.en: They would then log into Facebook and download an app.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会登录Facebook并下载一个应用程序。

sentences.en: And for taking this quiz, we'd get a small payment code.
sentences.zh: 为了参加这个测试，我们会得到一个小的支付代码。

sentences.en: That's how they would get paid.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们获得报酬的方式。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the app would scrape their data and all their friends' data.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，该应用程序会抓取他们的数据以及他们所有朋友的数据。

sentences.en: And that was, you know, basic bio data and what they had liked on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 那就是，你知道，基本的个人资料数据以及他们在Facebook上点赞的内容。

sentences.en: The researchers would use the answers that these people had provided on their personality quiz and their Facebook data to kind of create the algorithm that tells you if you're going to like the Wu-Tang Clan or,
sentences.zh: 研究人员会利用这些人提供的性格测试答案和他们的Facebook数据，来创建那个能告诉你是否会喜欢武当派或者，

sentences.en: you know, Hello Kitty or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Hello Kitty之类的算法。

sentences.en: And then once you felt that algorithm could predict that kind of thing with enough accuracy, you would then unleash it on the tens of millions of friends' profiles.
sentences.zh: 一旦你觉得该算法能以足够的准确度预测这类事情，你就会把它释放到数千万朋友的个人资料上。

sentences.en: For which you have no answers.
sentences.zh: 而你并没有这些人的答案。

sentences.en: You don't have the personality quiz answers.
sentences.zh: 你没有性格测试的答案。

sentences.en: Almost all this harvesting of data was done in June and July and a little bit of August 2014.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有这些数据抓取都是在2014年6月、7月和8月的一小部分时间里完成的。

sentences.en: And they came up with about 50 million profiles.
sentences.zh: 他们最终获得了大约5000万份个人资料。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: 50 million.
Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, this system seems to exploit the fact that you can get permission from just a few people.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个系统似乎利用了这样一个事实：你只需要获得少数人的许可。

sentences.en: And once you're in their world, you can then gather up all the information you need from their friends, which is the whole notion of Facebook anyway.
sentences.zh: 一旦你进入了他们的世界，你就可以从他们的朋友那里收集你需要的所有信息，这本来就是Facebook的整个运作逻辑。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, I think in all fairness to Facebook, while this was going on, they were already tightening up their permissions.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为公平地说，在Facebook方面，当这一切发生时，他们已经在收紧权限了。

sentences.en: In April 2014, new apps were no longer allowed to scrape friends like this.
sentences.zh: 2014年4月，新应用不再被允许以这种方式抓取好友数据。

sentences.en: But any apps that had already existed and Kogan's did exist were grandfathered in for another year.
sentences.zh: 但任何已经存在的应用程序——科根的程序确实存在——都被允许保留一年。

sentences.en: So, this was totally allowed by Facebook at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时，Facebook完全允许这样做。

sentences.en: You know, they could go in and take all this data.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们可以进去获取所有这些数据。

sentences.en: The thing is, you weren't supposed to give it to third parties.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，你本不应该把这些数据交给第三方。

sentences.en: You definitely were not supposed to say you were doing it for academic research and then hand it over to a political data firm that also has a commercial arm.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不应该声称是为了学术研究而获取数据，然后转手交给一家同时拥有商业部门的政治数据公司。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是个问题。

sentences.en: It's also a problem, you know, for the researcher who is an academic.
sentences.zh: 对于身为学者的研究人员来说，这也是个问题。

sentences.en: You know, there's not an academic study on Earth that allows you to deceive people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，世界上没有任何一项学术研究是允许你去欺骗人们的。

sentences.en: What do Chris and Cambridge Analytica ultimately get out of this?
sentences.zh: 克里斯和剑桥分析公司最终从这件事中得到了什么？

sentences.en: What do they learn by doing this research?
sentences.zh: 他们通过这项研究学到了什么？

sentences.en: They're getting the data they need to build the tools to get a psychological picture of tens of millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了构建工具所需的数据，从而勾勒出数千万美国人的心理画像。

sentences.en: And so, they're testing messages off this.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们正以此为基础测试各种信息。

sentences.en: They're saying, okay, we've got neurotic voters here.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，好吧，我们这里有神经质的选民。

sentences.en: Let's show them a wall.
sentences.zh: 让我们给他们展示一堵墙。

sentences.en: Let's show them people sneaking over a wall.
sentences.zh: 让我们给他们看有人偷偷翻越围墙的画面。

sentences.en: Like a wall with Mexico.
sentences.zh: 就像美墨边境的那种墙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Chris showed me some of these slides.
sentences.zh: 克里斯给我看了一些幻灯片。

sentences.en: Some of them are like, you see people coming in over a wall and it says like, there's more than one kind of national security leak.
sentences.zh: 其中一些画面显示人们翻越围墙，上面写着类似“国家安全漏洞不止一种”之类的话。

sentences.en: Stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的内容。

sentences.en: How can we appeal to people?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何吸引人们？

sentences.en: How can we appeal to their fears?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何利用他们的恐惧？

sentences.en: Most of it was fear-based from what I saw.
sentences.zh: 据我所见，大部分内容都是基于恐惧的。

sentences.en: There wasn't a whole lot of hope-based.
sentences.zh: 并没有多少基于希望的内容。

sentences.en: So, if you fit a particular kind of personality profile,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你符合某种特定的人格特征，

sentences.en: Cambridge Analytica is going to start to build messages and you're going to get served a particular kind of ad based on that.
sentences.zh: 剑桥分析公司就会开始为你定制信息，并根据这些特征向你推送特定的广告。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It's so interesting, this idea of using social media to tap into people's kind of primal desires and fears.
sentences.zh: 利用社交媒体来挖掘人们内心深处的原始欲望和恐惧，这个想法太有意思了。

sentences.en: It's the same tactics that we now know Russia used in the 2016 elections in their own effort to influence the results and to try to hurt Hillary Clinton and favor Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这与我们现在所知的俄罗斯在2016年大选中使用的策略如出一辙，他们当时也是为了影响选举结果，试图打击希拉里·克林顿并支持唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Chris starts telling you this whole story back in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯是在八月份开始向你讲述整个故事的。

sentences.en: Why do you think he came forward?
sentences.zh: 你认为他为什么会站出来？

sentences.en: He's being called now a whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 他现在被称为“吹哨人”。

sentences.en: But this whole thing was, in many ways, his idea, it sounded like.
sentences.zh: 但听起来，整件事在很多方面都是他的主意。

sentences.en: So, I think Chris was really wrestling with all this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为克里斯当时确实在进行激烈的思想斗争。

sentences.en: He had joined up as a 23, then a 24-year-old kid who was really into this idea of playing with psychographic research to kind of get to people and alter their views.
sentences.zh: 他加入时才23岁，后来24岁，当时他非常热衷于利用心理测绘研究来影响人们并改变他们的观点。

sentences.en: He was doing a PhD in kind of fashion and fashion marketing.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在攻读时尚和时尚营销方面的博士学位。

sentences.en: I remember the name.
sentences.zh: 我记得那个名字。

sentences.en: It was Mental Wear.
sentences.zh: 叫“心理穿戴”（Mental Wear）。

sentences.en: It was the name of his PhD thesis.
sentences.zh: 那是他博士论文的题目。

sentences.en: And he wanted to use the psychographic research to try and predict kind of consumer fashion choices.
sentences.zh: 他想利用心理测绘研究来预测消费者的时尚选择。

sentences.en: And he quipped to me.
sentences.zh: 他曾对我打趣说。

sentences.en: I remember sitting there saying, you know, he wanted to be in fashion, not fascism.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时坐在那儿，他说他想从事的是时尚（fashion），而不是法西斯主义（fascism）。

sentences.en: And I think he really saw the Bannons and Mercers and their ideas of the world as leading to fascism in a way that he found deeply abhorrent.
sentences.zh: 我认为他确实看出了班农、默瑟这些人及其世界观正在导致法西斯主义，这让他感到极其厌恶。

sentences.en: He left at the end of 2014.
sentences.zh: 他在2014年底离开了。

sentences.en: So, I think by then he knew what he was getting into, what he'd gotten into.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想那时他已经知道自己卷入了什么，以及自己陷入了怎样的境地。

sentences.en: They had dealt with a lot of pretty fringe right-wing American candidates.
sentences.zh: 他们曾与许多相当边缘的美国右翼候选人打过交道。

sentences.en: One of his colleagues told me about a moment when a bunch of evangelical Christians showed up.
sentences.zh: 他的一位同事曾告诉我，有一次一群福音派基督徒找上门来。

sentences.en: And this colleague was also gay.
sentences.zh: 而这位同事本人也是同性恋。

sentences.en: And they wanted to know the psychographic research was good for identifying homosexuals so they could message them to convert them to heterosexuality.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道心理测绘研究是否能有效识别同性恋者，以便他们能针对性地发送信息，将他们“转化为”异性恋。

sentences.en: So, I think these guys knew who they were dealing with here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这些人很清楚自己在和什么样的人打交道。

sentences.en: What happens after Chris tells you this story?
sentences.zh: 克里斯告诉你这个故事后发生了什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，最大的疑问是什么？

sentences.en: And where did you go next with the story?
sentences.zh: 接下来你又是如何跟进这个故事的？

sentences.en: So, Chris said he had a whole bunch of documents he wanted to show us.
sentences.zh: 克里斯说他有一大堆文件想给我们看。

sentences.en: We wanted to see those documents.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看那些文件。

sentences.en: The documents that showed the scale and scope of the data harvesting, that show Cambridge Analytica's involvement in it.
sentences.zh: 那些展示了数据采集规模和范围的文件，以及展示剑桥分析公司参与其中的证据。

sentences.en: And also documents that show what Facebook knew and what Facebook doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 还有一些文件显示了Facebook知道什么，以及Facebook不知道什么。

sentences.en: And what he's telling me is there are documents, including letters from Facebook, seeking to make sure this data has been deleted.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，确实存在一些文件，包括来自Facebook的信件，要求确保这些数据已被删除。

sentences.en: And like, wait, so Facebook knows that this amount of data has been harvested and it's never said a word publicly?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以Facebook知道有这么多数据被采集了，却从未公开说过一个字？

sentences.en: Because if they're asking for the data to be deleted, presumably they knew it had been harvested.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们要求删除数据，想必他们早就知道数据被采集了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And we now know Facebook shut down the app and they started investigating.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道Facebook关闭了那个应用程序并开始进行调查。

sentences.en: And throughout the first half of 2016, they were chasing down Kogan.
sentences.zh: 在2016年上半年，他们一直在追查科根。

sentences.en: They were chasing down Cambridge Analytica.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在追查剑桥分析公司。

sentences.en: They were chasing down Chris and others to try and get that data deleted.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在追查克里斯和其他人，试图让那些数据被删除。

sentences.en: In 2017, when reports started coming out with some figures about the data that was out there, Facebook still would just say, you know, what's taken care of?
sentences.zh: 2017年，当有关数据泄露规模的报道开始出现时，Facebook依然只是说，你知道，事情已经处理好了？

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Nothing to look at here.
sentences.zh: 没什么可看的。

sentences.en: And suddenly we're sitting with this guy who's got these documents that say, well, actually there is something to look at here.
sentences.zh: 而突然间，我们坐在了拥有这些文件的人面前，文件显示，好吧，实际上确实有问题。

sentences.en: There's a lot out there.
sentences.zh: 外面流出的数据非常多。

sentences.en: So these documents are making clear that Facebook knew this information had been taken, that it had been taken without permission.
sentences.zh: 所以这些文件清楚地表明，Facebook知道这些信息被窃取了，而且是在未经许可的情况下被窃取的。

sentences.en: And from everything you can tell, they do not alert the people from whom it was taken without their permission.
sentences.zh: 据你所知，他们并没有通知那些在未经许可的情况下被窃取信息的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, they did not alert them.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，他们没有通知这些人。

sentences.en: And one of the things about this data set, if this psychographic research actually works, it's not something you need to update every few years.
sentences.zh: 关于这个数据集，如果心理测绘研究真的有效，它就不需要每隔几年更新一次。

sentences.en: You know, people's positions on gun control or taxes may change.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们在枪支管制或税收问题上的立场可能会改变。

sentences.en: But if you're neurotic at 24, you're neurotic at 44.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在24岁时是神经质的，那么你在44岁时依然是神经质的。

sentences.en: Maybe you've moderated your personality, but personality is a constant.
sentences.zh: 也许你的性格变得温和了一些，但性格本身是恒定的。

sentences.en: So the data is good for decades, presumably.
sentences.zh: 所以这些数据在几十年内都是有效的，想必如此。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So this is what you're arguing, kind of a lifetime's worth of psychographic information about tens of millions of voters.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你的论点，关于数千万选民的心理测绘信息，其价值可能伴随终身。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So do you go to Facebook with this information?
sentences.zh: 那么你拿着这些信息去找Facebook了吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, we went to them more than a week before the story was supposed to publish.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在报道发表前一周多就去找过他们。

sentences.en: And Facebook decided, knowing this story was going to come out, they decided to preemptively put up their own statement and say, you know, we're going to come clean.
sentences.zh: Facebook在知道报道即将发布的情况下，决定先发制人地发表声明，说他们要“坦白从宽”。

sentences.en: This happened and we're trying to get to the bottom of it and really present themselves as proactive.
sentences.zh: 他们声称事情已经发生，他们正在努力查明真相，并试图表现得非常主动。

sentences.en: When they, in fact, hadn't been that proactive.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，他们并没有那么主动。

sentences.en: It's hard to see somebody as proactive when they're putting out statements about what they're doing and to fix something.
sentences.zh: 当一家公司在报道发布前不到24小时才发表声明说正在修复问题，很难让人觉得他们是主动的。

sentences.en: Less than 24 hours before they know a story that includes all these details is going to be published.
sentences.zh: 而那篇报道包含了所有这些细节。

sentences.en: Which seems more like saving face, potentially, than actually fixing it.
sentences.zh: 这看起来更像是为了挽回面子，而不是真的在解决问题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Matt, what's happening now?
sentences.zh: 马特，现在情况如何？

sentences.en: What's been the result of all this reporting and Chris's decision to come forward and talk?
sentences.zh: 所有这些报道以及克里斯决定站出来讲述真相，带来了什么结果？

sentences.en: All hells are sort of broken loose for Facebook.
sentences.zh: Facebook可以说是乱成了一锅粥。

sentences.en: You know, their stock has lost nearly $50 billion in the last two days.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的股价在过去两天里蒸发了近500亿美元。

sentences.en: They've got lawmakers in both the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国和英国的议员们都在要求马克·扎克伯格出席听证会。

sentences.en: and Britain calling for Mark Zuckerberg to come testify.
sentences.zh: 纽约州和马萨诸塞州的州检察长也开启了调查。

sentences.en: They've got state attorney generals in New York and Massachusetts opening up investigations.
sentences.zh: 我认为对他们来说，这正演变成一场真正的危机：我们到底是一家什么样的公司？

sentences.en: And I think for them it's becoming this real crisis of, you know, what kind of company are we?
sentences.zh: 人们是如何看待我们的？

sentences.en: How do people see us?
sentences.zh: 我们能做些什么来补救？

sentences.en: And what can we do to fix it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他们的商业模式吗？

sentences.en: You know, is this their business model?
sentences.zh: 我认为人们一直把Facebook当作一个有趣的地方。

sentences.en: I think people, you know, have thought of Facebook as a fun place.
sentences.zh: 你把孩子的照片发上去。

sentences.en: You know, you throw your kids' pictures up there.
sentences.zh: 你就像个乡村歌手或嘻哈艺人一样。

sentences.en: You're kind of like a country star or a hip-hop guy.
sentences.zh: 你向人们讲述你的生活。

sentences.en: And you tell people about your life.
sentences.zh: 而他们现在意识到的是，当你向人们讲述你的生活时，他们可能会试图操纵你。

sentences.en: And what they're realizing now is that when you tell people about their life, they can try and manipulate you.
sentences.zh: 他们会寻找你的弱点，然后向你推销东西，无论是新夹克还是某种政治观点。

sentences.en: They can look for ways to find your vulnerabilities and either sell you something, whether it's, you know, a new jacket or a political idea.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让很多人感到害怕。

sentences.en: And I think that's something that scares a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些事情——我不认为人们习惯于生活在一个存在大规模监控的世界里。

sentences.en: You know, there's something – I don't think people are used to living in a world where there's massive surveillance.
sentences.zh: 人们认为监控就是摄像头和监听电话。

sentences.en: And people think of surveillance as cameras and people listen to your phone.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，更多的是把你的一切放到Facebook上，让一家巨头公司掌握这些信息。

sentences.en: But mostly it's putting your stuff on Facebook and letting a giant company know about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个能让人们深刻意识到这一点的故事。

sentences.en: And I think this is one of those stories that helps bring that home to people.
sentences.zh: 这并不是唯一的故事。

sentences.en: It's not the only story.
sentences.zh: 这也不是什么新观点。

sentences.en: This is not a new idea.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个让人们开始思考的时刻。

sentences.en: But it is one of those moments where people are thinking that.
sentences.zh: 对于像Facebook这样的公司来说，这确实代表了一场真正的危机。

sentences.en: And for a company like Facebook, it does represent a real crisis.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，剑桥分析公司也陷入了困境。

sentences.en: At the same time, Cambridge Analytica is reeling.
sentences.zh: 他们先是遭遇了我们的报道，紧接着英国第四频道新闻台也进行了跟进报道，

sentences.en: They had our stories, and that's been immediately followed up by Channel 4 News in Britain,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉《独立报》，他们也进行了自己的调查，派了一名记者伪装成来自斯里兰卡的潜在客户，想要雇佣剑桥分析公司帮助他们的政治盟友在斯里兰卡赢得选举。

sentences.en: which told the Independent of Us had done their own investigation where they had sent one of the reporters posing as a prospective client from Sri Lanka who wanted to hire Cambridge to kind of help their political allies win elections in Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 他们用隐藏摄像机拍到了首席执行官亚历山大·尼克斯，他告诉这个假客户，我们可以去对付你的竞争对手。

sentences.en: And they have Alexander Nix, the CEO, on a secret camera they were using where he's telling this fake client that, you know, well, we can go after your rivals.
sentences.zh: 我们可以利用人去给他们行贿，或者派女人去诱捕他们，我们可以秘密拍摄这一切，然后放到互联网上。

sentences.en: We can use people to pass bribes to them or send women to entrap them, and we can secretly film it all and then put it on the internet.
sentences.zh: 对于一家被美国总统大选获胜候选人雇佣的公司来说，其首席执行官说出这种话真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: That's a pretty remarkable thing for the CEO of a company that was hired by the winning candidate in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，他今天被停职了。

sentences.en: presidential election.
sentences.zh: 所以剑桥分析公司的首席执行官不再掌权了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was suspended today.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the CEO of Cambridge Analytica is no longer in charge.
sentences.zh: 你认为这个故事接下来的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 你现在对什么感兴趣？

sentences.en: What do you think that the next questions are in this story?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，剑桥分析公司所做的事情，结果发现并不难。

sentences.en: What are you interested in now?
sentences.zh: 它不需要任何特殊的许可，特别是在2014年和2015年之前。

sentences.en: So, you know, what Cambridge Analytica did, turns out it wasn't very hard.
sentences.zh: 那么还有多少人在做同样的事情？

sentences.en: It didn't take any kind of special permission, especially before 2014 and 2015.
sentences.zh: 他们中有多少人拥有更多的时间、更多的资金，而且做得更好？

sentences.en: So how many other people were doing it?
sentences.zh: 他们对我们了解多少？

sentences.en: How many of them had more time, had more money, and were just better at it?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And how much do they know about us?
sentences.zh: 马特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 不客气，伙计。

sentences.en: Matt, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure, man.
sentences.zh: 我与普京总统通了电话，祝贺他赢得选举，他的选举胜利。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 周二在白宫举行的新闻发布会上，

sentences.en: I had a call with President Putin and congratulated him on the victory, his electoral victory.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统描述了他与弗拉基米尔·普京之间的一次热情的电话交谈，谈到了他作为俄罗斯总统的压倒性连任。

sentences.en: During a news conference at the White House on Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 特朗普没有询问普京关于投票公正性的问题，也没有提及有关俄罗斯在英国毒害一名前间谍的报道，或是俄罗斯干预2016年大选的问题。

sentences.en: President Trump described a warm telephone conversation with Vladimir Putin about his overwhelming re-election as Russia's president.
sentences.zh: 总统在电话中没有提出俄罗斯干预选举的问题吗？

sentences.en: Trump did not ask Putin about the fairness of the vote, reports that Russia poisoned a former spy in Britain, or Russia's meddling in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 我不认为在这次特定的通话中提到了这一点，

sentences.en: Did the president not raise the issue of Russian election meddling in that phone call?
sentences.zh: 但这是我们已经广泛讨论过的问题，我们也在继续寻找方法和步骤，确保此类事件不再发生。

sentences.en: I don't believe it came up on this specific call,
sentences.zh: 相反，总统专注于白宫所称的“共同利益”，包括朝鲜、乌克兰以及美俄之间不断升级的军备竞赛。

sentences.en: but it is something that we've spoken extensively about and continue to look at ways and steps forward to make sure it never happens again.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一次非常好的通话，我怀疑我们可能在不久的将来会面，讨论正在失控的军备竞赛。

sentences.en: Instead, the president focused on what the White House called shared interests, including North Korea, Ukraine, and the escalating arms race between the United States and Russia.
sentences.zh: 周二，第二名声称与特朗普总统有染的女性提起诉讼，要求解除一项要求她保持沉默的法律协议。

sentences.en: We had a very good call, and I suspect that we'll probably be meeting in the not-too-distant future to discuss the arms race, which is getting out of control.
sentences.zh: 这名女性是一位名叫凯伦·麦克杜格尔的《花花公子》模特，她说自己被拥有《国家询问报》的公司误导了。

sentences.en: And a second woman claiming to have had an affair with President Trump filed a lawsuit on Tuesday seeking to be released from a legal agreement requiring her silence.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个值得关注的问题。

sentences.en: The woman, a playboy model named Karen McDougal, says she was misled by the company that owns the National Enquirer,
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待后续发展。

sentences.en: which paid her $150,000 in return for not discussing the relationship.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，她获得了15万美元的封口费，条件是不得讨论这段关系。

sentences.en: Her lawsuit comes two weeks after Stephanie Clifford, an adult film actress, challenged a similar confidentiality agreement.
sentences.zh: 在她提起诉讼的两周前，成人电影女演员斯蒂芬妮·克利福德也对一份类似的保密协议提出了质疑。

sentences.en: Both women claim their contracts are invalid, and that they should be free to describe their experiences with the president.
sentences.zh: 两位女性都声称她们的合同无效，并表示她们应该有权自由描述自己与总统的经历。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
